binders: A finite index type ι, which may be empty.
A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with the assertion that μ is a probability measure.
A finite family X = (X_i) indexed by ι, where each X_i : Ω → ℝ.
hypotheses: For every i in ι, X_i is Borel measurable.
For every i in ι, X_i is μ-integrable and ∫ X_i dμ = 0.
For every i in ι, |X_i(ω)| ≤ K for μ-almost every ω.
The family of functions (X_i) indexed by ι is mutually independent with respect to μ.
conclusions: Let V = ∑_{i∈ι} ∫Ω X_i(ω)^2 dμ(ω). Then μ({ω ∈ Ω | |∑_{i∈ι} X_i(ω)| ≥ t}), converted to a real number, is at most 2 exp(-(t²/2)/(V + Kt/3)).
Equivalently when the denominator is nonzero, the upper bound is 2 exp(-t²/(2(V + Kt/3))).
mathematical_definitions: The full finite sum is S(ω) = ∑_{i∈ι} X_i(ω).
The second-moment sum is V = ∑_{i∈ι} ∫Ω X_i(ω)^2 dμ(ω).
The notation μ.real(A) means ENNReal.toReal(μ(A)); for a probability measure this is the ordinary real-valued probability of A.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of mutually independent, measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables on a probability space, if every variable has absolute value at most the same positive constant K almost surely, then for every nonnegative t the probability that the absolute value of their sum is at least t is bounded above by 2 exp(-(t²/2)/(∑_i E[X_i²] + Kt/3)).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is only assumed finite, not nonempty. If it is empty, both finite sums are zero and the statement remains meaningful.
The bound |X_i| ≤ K is only μ-almost everywhere, not pointwise.
The same positive constant K bounds every member of the family.
The conclusion is stated only for t ≥ 0.
No explicit variance notation is used. The denominator contains ∑_i ∫X_i² dμ; because each mean is zero, these second moments coincide mathematically with the variances.

Lean real division is totalized: division by zero evaluates to zero. The denominator V + Kt/3 can be zero in the degenerate case t = 0 and V = 0; then the formal right-hand side is 2, so the conclusion is still meaningful and trivial for a probability measure.
The theorem gives an upper bound that can exceed 1; it is not truncated by min(1, ·).
The event is the two-sided absolute-deviation event for the sum, not a one-sided event.
Independence is asserted for the entire indexed family through iIndepFun, not merely pairwise independence.
